body:
alex: CI red on hosted-integ against Hosted API — multiple tests failing on shard 9 (auth handshake + streaming toolcall + schema ordering). stack: staging/latest. Anyone free to triage?

maria: saw the alert. I can take an initial look in ~30m. Which CI job? link: https://ci.redwood.example/runs/7234

alex: job is hosted-integ/shard-9. Root failure: auth handshake times out, then a cascade of streaming timeouts when tool-call payloads are attempted.

ci-bot: Build failed: hosted-integ/shard-9 (run 7234) — 7 failing tests. Artifacts: https://ci.redwood.example/artifacts/7234/logs.tar.gz :warning:

sam: quick glance at logs: the auth handshake shows 401 -> then jwks fetch retries hitting 429. excerpt: 
```
AuthHandshakeError: missing kid in JWKS (received empty keys)
2026-03-15T12:03:21Z fetch_jwks 429 rate_limited
stream: toolcall start -> grpc DEADLINE_EXCEEDED after 15s
```

jen_oncall: is this near any recent merges? maybe the jwks cache change from #4352?

ben: yep #4352 touched jwks caching TTL and the fallback fetch path. It landed yesterday in canary. Could be our canary rollout pushed to staging shards.

alex: ok can we rerun shard-9 with higher logging and skip cache layer? If repro, bisect between before/after #4352.

maria: /rerun hosted-integ/shard-9 with env JWKS_OVER_LOG=1 and RERUN_REASON="triage-auth-handshake"

ci-bot: Rerun triggered: hosted-integ/shard-9 (rerun 7234.1) by maria — started.

sam: also add a targeted unit: auth/jwks_fetch_test — it was flaky in local. If that isolates to jwks client, we save time.

alex: pinging @jen_oncall for canary config: do we have rollout id for staging that would affect shard 9?

jen_oncall: staging rollout id r-2026-03-14-18:00 includes jwks-ttl bump but only 20% canary. Unexpected it hit shard 9 fully. I'll check orchestration logs.

ben: I can start a quick bisect: schedule two runs (pre-#4352 sha, post-#4352 sha) on shard-9 subset. If post is red and pre is green, we narrow it.

maria: rerun finished — same 401 + fetch 429 pattern, so probably runtime fetch path. logs: https://ci.redwood.example/artifacts/7234.1/logs/handshake.txt

sam: adding a local repro note: running auth/jwks_fetch_test locally with jittered rate-limit sim reproduces 429 -> empty keys on our current client when cache.ttl=0. Might explain flake.

alex: next actions: (1) bisect with both shas (ben), (2) temp rollback of jwks change on staging or adjust rate-limit backoff (jen), (3) add guard in client to treat 429 as retry-with-backoff and not return empty keys (maria/sam).

jen_oncall: I'll pause canary and open an emergency patch to increase backoff. tagging infra to keep an eye on production. :eyes:

ben: bisect queued: pre-sha 6a99c3 (before #4352) run 7240, post-sha f2b1d7 (after #4352) run 7241. I'll report when done.

ci-bot: Build 7240 (pre) — success on shard-9 subset. Build 7241 (post) — reproduces auth handshake fail.

maria: confirms regression introduced by #4352. I'll draft a quick revert/patch and a proper fix for robust jwks fetch.

sam: optional short-term mitigation: add inequality check so empty jwks keys triggers a fetch retry instead of immediate fail. small patch, low risk.

alex: thanks all — if someone posts a PR link I can review quickly. Also add a short blurb to the incident channel when we have rollback/patch plan.

maria: opening PR now: https://git.redwood/pr/4368 — revert ttl change + added retry guard.

jen_oncall: rolling the patch to staging canary now, will watch shard-9.

ci-bot: PR 4368 CI: running.

ben: once CI green on 4368 we'll merge and promote. Good catch everyone. :thumbsup:
